title: FitSM
lead: A lightweight, free ITSM standard — designed to make service management achievable for federations of organisations and smaller IT teams.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body: FitSM is an open, freely available standard for lightweight IT service management, published and maintained by ITEMO (IT Service Management Expert Group). Originally developed through the EU-funded FedSM project, it was designed to make structured service management accessible in federated IT infrastructures — such as research networks, public sector consortia, and cloud federations — where multiple organisations share responsibility for service delivery. FitSM is aligned with ISO/IEC 20000 and shares conceptual roots with ITIL, but strips away complexity to focus on what is strictly necessary to deliver and improve IT services.

sections.heading: ITOM Perspective
sections.body: FitSM is relevant in ITOM engagements where a full ITIL implementation would be disproportionate — for example in smaller organisations, government agencies with limited ITSM maturity, or multi-provider environments where a common, lightweight baseline is needed across organisational boundaries. Its federated design makes it particularly suited to SIAM contexts, where a shared process model must span multiple providers without imposing heavy governance overhead. FitSM can also serve as a stepping stone: organisations adopt it to establish discipline and then mature towards ISO/IEC 20000 or ITIL 4 over time.

items.desc: FitSM was purpose-built for environments where IT services are delivered across organisational boundaries — a direct fit for SIAM and multi-provider models
covering the full ITSM lifecycle from strategy through operation and improvement, at a pragmatic level of detail
all FitSM standards, templates, and training materials are publicly available at no cost — lowering the adoption barrier significantly
FitSM is structurally aligned with the ISO/IEC 20000 standard, making it a viable path towards formal certification
FitSM deliberately limits prescriptiveness — requirements are achievable rather than aspirational, enabling real-world adoption in resource-constrained settings

items.term: SMS — Service Management System Planning and Control
items.desc: establishes and maintains the management system itself
manages the portfolio of services across their full lifecycle
agrees and monitors service levels with customers
manages external suppliers and underpinning contracts

items.term: Fin — Financial Management for IT Services
items.desc: tracks costs and budgets associated with IT service delivery
ensures sufficient capacity to meet agreed service levels

items.term: ISRM — Information Security and Privacy Management
items.desc: protects the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of information

items.term: SACM — Service Availability and Continuity Management
items.desc: manages availability targets and recovery capabilities
controls changes to minimise disruption to services
manages the build, test, and deployment of releases
maintains accurate information about service components and their relationships

items.term: INC — Incident and Service Request Management
items.desc: restores services and fulfils standard requests efficiently
addresses root causes to prevent recurring incidents
builds and maintains productive relationships with customers and stakeholders
FitSM adoption assessment — evaluate readiness and identify the right scope of FitSM processes for the organisation
Lightweight ITSM design — implement a proportionate process set based on FitSM for smaller or federated environments
FitSM-to-ISO/IEC 20000 roadmap — plan the maturation journey from FitSM baseline towards formal certification
Multi-provider baseline design — use FitSM as the common process model in SIAM and multi-sourcing contexts
